# Dependency graph for the attained extremal cap stress

This is a dependency map of proved intermediate results, not a proof of OC.
The proposed sharp multiplier estimate at the end is explicitly unproved.

## A. Obtaining an actual extremal family

A1. Fixed finite lattice-convex P with an interior integer z_0 and positive
mixed volume has a positive central fiber. Self-contained determinant-one
normalization, positive barycentric weights, and one affine fiber shear
bound every fiber and every nonaffine center displacement.

A2. Hausdorff limits preserve actual fibers on P. Fiber measures converge in
TV, and same-fiber slab estimates make maximized depth continuous, including
oblique and vertical halfspaces.

A3. Inner polytopal approximation preserves P and converges in depth. For
any strict counterexample choose a finite positive-fiber facet bound N that
still admits a strict counterexample.

A4. The class with <=N facets per positive fiber, allowing arbitrary zero-
volume fibers, is closed and compact after A1. It has an attained minimizer
below the threshold. Either zero-volume fibers give an exact smaller-
projection support reduction, or all fibers are positive polytopes.

Sources: `candidate a14cc5f809b2b766`,
`candidate 21db6cba533d25dc`.

## B. Exact critical circuits and a bounded relevant group count

B1. Boundary points of fibers and points in zero-volume fibers have depth
zero. Supporting faces and a large finite exposing integer normal prove
this without discarding boundary fibers.

B2. Directional capacities with unit continuous normal attain their integer-
normal infima and are continuous. Finite affine-threshold compactification
realizes all finite/infinite threshold limits by actual ambient halfspaces.

B3. Every positive fiber has an interior restricted maximizer. Active
continuous normals balance; a minimal positive circuit of <=d+1 caps through
that maximizer covers the entire continuous fiber. Every cap has exactly
the restricted maximum's mass.

B4. Each circuit's projected halfspace G_i contains its anchor and certifies
whole-fiber coverage wherever G_i holds. Relative Doignon selects <=2^n
whole groups covering P. The selected deepest-origin groups cover every
deepest integer fiber.

B5. Add all nondeep local groups, whose budgets are strict slack. Assign
deepest indices to selected groups and nondeep indices to their own added
groups. This preserves <=2^n groups that can possibly have active budgets.

Sources: `candidate b989614dc4f86228`,
`candidate 5e600a897e2488c6`, Section 1.
The alternative exact <=2^n(d+1) closed-cap-cover compactification in the
first note is independently valid but is NOT needed for B3--B5.

## C. A genuine joint maximum-volume problem

C1. Use support-function coordinates respecting each fiber's own small-
erosion fan. Support convexity and actual fiber compatibility are finitely
many homogeneous linear inequalities; these perturbations preserve the
facet bound N.

C2. For each assigned p impose the linear coverage inequality
sum_j rho_ij(v_ij.p-b_ij)>=0. Keep rho positive and allow the cap coefficients
to vary, with sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0. These conditions guarantee P x R^d is
covered for EVERY feasible parameter choice.

C3. The attained depth minimizer is an actual maximum of total volume under
these coverage conditions and fixed cap budgets beta M. A feasible increase
of total volume would strictly lower its normalized depth.

Sources: `candidate 94a1565e143d393e` (cone only),
`candidate 21a9da879344205f`, `candidate 5e600a897e2488c6`.

## D. Normalized global stress, with boundary traces

D1. Facet-prism derivatives give volume and cap first variations. With fixed
continuous normals, a coincident facet has a common theta in [0,1] in all
shape/threshold/integer-normal terms. With rotating normals it requires a
measurable theta(x); its mass and first moments form a compact convex set.

D2. Common inner parallel erosion preserves actual compatibility and leaves
all coverage constraints unchanged. It pairs strictly negatively with every
active cap-gradient possibility, since every active cap has a positive
boundary patch inside its open halfspace.

D3. Finite-dimensional separation (with a proved closed-cone argument in
the moment-set case) gives an objective-normalized stress. There are no
abnormal objective-zero multipliers. The cap multipliers lambda and
coverage multipliers eta are nonnegative and use the SAME facet traces.

Sources: `candidate 21a9da879344205f`,
`candidate cda9653e9d3e6d40`, Sections 1--3.

## E. Exact equations and contact support

E1. Threshold and integer-normal stationarity give
lambda_ij S_ij=rho_ij t_i and
lambda_ij Z_ij=rho_ij sum_p eta_ip p, with t_i=sum_p eta_ip.
Slack groups have lambda=eta=0. In every nonzero group all lambda_ij>0.

E2. Eta is supported on deepest assigned integer fibers and active projected
coverage equalities. Every deepest center at each such index lies on every
cap plane of its assigned group.

E3. Joint homothety or the explicit offset calculation gives
sum_ij lambda_ij=1/beta exactly, with <=2^n nonzero groups.

E4. Joint continuous-normal variation gives
lambda_ij X_ij=rho_ij q_i. Hence all cap sections in a stressed group have
one full effective centroid (sum_p eta_ip p/t_i,q_i/t_i), lying in C and
on all group planes. For k_i=d+1 it equals an eta-weighted convex combination
of actual deepest centers. For deficient circuits equality is proved only
modulo the common kernel of the continuous normals. Varying rho adds no
geometric freedom after positive rescaling of each cap's coefficients.

Sources: `candidate 5e600a897e2488c6`,
`candidate cda9653e9d3e6d40`.

## Exact unresolved quantitative step

The established equations reduce the desired bound on this extremal branch
to controlling the group multiplier sums

    sum_j lambda_ij = t_i sum_j rho_ij/S_ij.

A bound <=1/gamma_d for each nonzero group would imply beta>=gamma_d/2^n,
but it has NOT been proved. It is not being included among the lemmas.
Nor has an alternative summation bound sufficient for OC been proved.
The hollow-projection branch and the common-kernel issue in deficient
circuits also require their own complete arguments if this route is used.
